summary: Intermittent dedicated throughput sag caused by ephemeral tenant spillover and slot unfairness
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Nimbus Analytics is observing repeated p50/p99 throughput degradation on their dedicated pool during mid-day windows. The degradation corresponds with a flurry of many short-lived, high-frequency client streams from a single tenant (internal batch job) that intermittently saturates slot allocation and triggers autoscaler churn.

Impact:
- Customer reports ~30-45% reduction in sustained throughput for their latency-sensitive routes for ~10-30 minute episodes.
- Affects production inference for multiple pinned models.
- Customer business impact: inference backlog and degraded feature availability for end users during peak window.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-nimbus-usw2-5 (reserved cluster)
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Khan: Initial report received from customer at 09:12 UTC. Attached their p99/per-route graphs and request IDs for one of the affected windows.
2026-03-10 - Ravi Menon: Triage started. I see correlated autoscaler scaling-up/spike logs for dp-nimbus-usw2-5 at 09:08-09:22 UTC. Opening investigation and pulling cluster allocation traces.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Marta Lopez): Observed many ephemeral connections from tenant "nimbus-batch" with avg duration 9s and very high inter-arrival rate. Prefetch subsystem shows repeated prefetch/evict cycles; kv-cache growth for other tenants stalls during these windows.

2026-03-12 - Eng (Ravi Menon): Implemented temporary mitigation: throttled tenant via rate-limit rule and applied an emergency affinity soft-evict to rebalance slots. Early telemetry shows throughput restored to ~95% baseline within 8 minutes of the action.
2026-03-12 - Customer (Nimbus Ops): Confirming recovered performance in their dashboards. They request explanation and permanent fix options.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and observations:
- 2026-03-10 09:05 UTC: first small-stream flood starts. Client telemetry indicates a tenant job that spins up thousands of short streams to multiple routes.
- 09:07-09:12 UTC: autoscaler interprets higher request rate and attempts to expand GPU allocation; due to slot granularity new GPUs are attached and background prefetchers start filling KV cache for hot models.
- 09:12-09:18 UTC: eviction/rehydration thrash: ephemeral tenant streams frequently tear down slot affinity leading to serialization of batchers and GPU slot fragmentation. Other tenants (including Nimbus customer production routes) see increased queueing and a drop in realized batch sizes.
- 09:18-09:25 UTC: autoscaler overshoots and then retracts, leaving fragmented slots and temporary GPU attachment churn.

Key signals pulled:
- Serving-runtime logs: repeated "slot-unavailable" and "batch-flush-from-eviction" messages correlated to tenant id nimbus-batch.
resolution:
Mitigation steps taken:
1) Applied tenant-scoped rate-limit to the offending tenant (nimbus-batch) to cap short-stream concurrency.
2) Executed emergency soft-evict for ephemeral tenant allocations to force consolidation and permit fair slot assignment.
3) Applied temporary autoscaler param adjustment: increased stabilization window from 30s to 90s for dp-nimbus-usw2-5 to reduce oscillatory attach/detach during short bursts.

Outcome:
- Post-mitigation telemetry (09:28 UTC onwards) shows customer throughput returned to ~95% of baseline and p99 latency improved. No longer triggering autoscaler rapid attach/detach loop.

Permanent follow-ups (action items):
- Ops: schedule tenant throttling rule in policy engine for all dedicated pools vulnerable to short-stream floods (ticket INT-43821, created).
- Eng: evaluate prefetch and KV-cache eviction heuristic to avoid aggressive fill during transient short-stream floods (RFC by 2026-03-20).
- Product: contact customer with options: quota limits, dedicated route rate-limits, or migration to a smaller-isolated pool for bursty batch jobs.
- Monitoring: add alert for slot fragmentation ratio > 0.25 and autoscaler attach/retract frequency > 3/min for dedicated pools.

We will keep this ticket open until permanent mitigation is scheduled or Nimbus accepts recommended changes.
